title: Classic Poutine Feed for the Crew
displayTitle: Classic Poutine Feed for the Crew
seoTitle: Classic Poutine Feed for the Crew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Double-fried fries with beef gravy and cheese curds for ten
subtitle: Double-fried fries with beef gravy and cheese curds for ten
description: Russet potatoes are cut thick, fried twice until shatter-crisp, then topped with hot beef gravy and squeaky cheese curds. Serve immediately on platters because poutine waits for no one—not even the captain.

steps.title: Cut and soak fries
steps.instruction: Cut potatoes into thick fries, soak in cold water 30 minutes, then drain and dry completely on towels.

steps.title: First fry
steps.instruction: Blanch fries in 325°F oil 4–5 minutes until soft but not browned. Drain, cool on racks at least 20 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 325°F.

steps.title: Build beef gravy
steps.instruction: Melt drippings, whisk in flour, cook 2 minutes, then whisk in broth, Worcestershire, and garlic powder. Simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Second fry
steps.instruction: Fry blanched potatoes at 375°F until deep golden and crisp, 3–4 minutes. Drain, salt immediately. Target oven/smoker temperature: 375°F.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.instruction: Pile hot fries on platters, scatter curds, ladle hot gravy over top, and serve at once with pepper mills on the table.

proTips: If curds are unavailable, use whole-milk mozzarella torn into chunks—never pre-shredded.
A splash of apple cider vinegar in gravy adds Quebec-style tang.
Vent the fryer area—poutine night smokes up the hall fast.
tonightSpread: Classic poutine platters with extra gravy on the side.
Simple vinegar coleslaw to cut the richness between bites.
leftovers: Honestly? Leftover poutine is a lost cause—plan portions tight.
Save gravy for hot beef sandwiches the next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Poutine is the ultimate Canadian hall comfort food. Crisp fries, rich gravy, and melting curds hit every craving after a cold call. This is the real deal—no poached eggs, no pulled pork gimmicks.
mealPrepNotes: Par-fry potatoes earlier in the day and finish-fry at service. Gravy must be hot enough to soften curds but not so hot it breaks them to mush. Work in batches so fries stay crisp.
